names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 30 decembrie, «Sfântul Cuvios Zotic», with the rank words left off; the page it links for his life is titled for «Sfântul Cuvios Zotic, hrănitorul de leproși», which is where the English epithet comes from.

Read out of saint.gr's line for 31 Δεκεμβρίου, «Άγιος Ζωτικός ο Ορφανοτρόφος», with the rank and the by-name left off. The by-name the Greek gives him, Ορφανοτρόφος, the feeder of orphans, is not the one the Romanian calendar gives him, and neither is stored as part of the name.

Read out of the Охридски пролог's third heading for 31. децембар ст. ст., „Преподобни мученик Зотик Сиропитатељ (хранитељ убогих).“ — «Преподобни мученик» is rank and §6 keeps it out; «Сиропитатељ», the feeder of orphans, is the by-name the heading gives him and is kept; and the parenthesis «(хранитељ убогих)», feeder of the destitute, is the book's own gloss on that by-name and not a second name, so it is left out. THE BARE «Зотик» WAS REFUSED DELIBERATELY: `fk.mjs` returns three holders for it — `zoticus-20-april`, `zoticus-of-nicomedia` and `zoticus-of-the-ten-of-crete` — and `corpus-gate.mjs` already carries a read `READ_FOLDS` key for those three at that exact width, so a bare form here would have widened a fold another reader wrote and read. The full string has no other holder at all.

Name page of days.pravoslavie.ru for this memory is «Зотик Сиропитатель, Константинопольский, пресвитер, сщмч.»: «пресвитер» and «сщмч.» are rank words and are stripped, and both epithets kept. `fk.mjs` on the stored string returns NONE; the folder’s Serbian «Зотик Сиропитатељ» folds elsewhere.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 30 декабря ст. ст. — «Сщмч. Зотика пресвитера, сиропитателя (IV).»

attestations.note: The day’s second entry. THE DAY IS NOT THE SAME IN EVERY CALENDAR: the folder’s Romanian row keeps him on 30 December and its Greek and Serbian rows on 31 December, and this calendar’s is 30 December, which is what is recorded. The line’s «Сщмч.» is a hieromartyr where the folder’s `types` read `venerable` and `martyr`; nothing was changed, because the three other calendars that made this folder gave it those words and the disagreement is the sources’ own. «сиропитателя» is the feeder of orphans, which is the epithet the folder’s display name already renders. NO `dates` WERE WRITTEN: the line’s «(IV)» is a bare Roman numeral and this wave has declined to write a date off one. ONE HYMN TAKEN, a proper kontakion naming him; the day prints no troparion for him and the folder had no hymn at all.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 30 decembrie — «Sfântul Cuvios Zotic»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 31ης Δεκεμβρίου — «Άγιος Ζωτικός ο Ορφανοτρόφος»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 31 Δεκεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», which is **one day later than the 30 decembrie the folder keeps on the Romanian calendar** — and that is two churches' own days and not a disagreement to be resolved, so each row carries its own. The entry is the same man beyond doubt: born and brought up at Rome of a noble family, called to the new capital by Constantine the Great, distinguished above all in the care of lepers, ill-used after Constantine's death by his son Constantius, and dead of the hardships. The folder's Romanian life tells the same story from doxologia.ro, down to the emperor's order that lepers be thrown into the sea and the gold Zoticus asked for to buy pearls. The Greek page adds what came after: that his death moved Constantius to repentance, that the emperor honoured his memory by building a leprosarium and endowing it with many estates and revenues, and that later emperors — «ο Κωνσταντίνος Ζ' ο Πορφυρογέννητος (945 μ.Χ.), ο Ιωάννης ο Τσιμισκής (963 - 976 μ.Χ.), ο Ρωμανός ο Γ' (1028 - 1034 μ.Χ.)» — saw to its working, so that it served a multitude of lepers through the saint's first act of mercy. It dates Constantine's call to Constantinople «(330 μ.Χ.)» but gives no year for Zoticus's own birth or death, so no `dates` object is proposed. The `related` row is Constantine the Great, whom the page makes the occasion of his whole work. It prints no hymn. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 13.01.2026 (31. децембар ст. ст.) — „Преподобни мученик Зотик Сиропитатељ (хранитељ убогих).“

attestations.note: The day's third entry. The identification is the house for the destitute, the lepers he took into it, Constantine the Great and the manner of death together, all of which the folder's own life already tells; the Greek keeps him on this same 31 December and the Romanian on the 30th. The serbian row was `undocumented`, so the row lands here. `types` UNTOUCHED: «Преподобни мученик» is the `venerable` and the `martyr` the folder already carries, in the one word `venerable-martyr` would have been — and no `types` row was changed, since both grades are present already. `dates`: THE FOLDER'S `dates` WAS NULL AND THIS ENTRY GIVES IT ITS FIRST DATE OF ANY KIND, a death in the fourth century off «Пострада у IV веку», which takes the folder out of the undated tray. NO `locations`. NO NEW `related`: `constantine-the-great` is already here and the entry confirms him in words, «Лични познаник цара Константина Великог», his personal acquaintance; the son «Констанције» who had him killed is no folder this corpus holds and stays in the book's Cyrillic. WHAT THE BOOK ADDS: that he was notable by birth and by rank; that he moved to Constantinople, cast off everything worldly and took holy orders; THAT HE PUT THE PLAGUE-STRICKEN INTO THE HOUSE HE FOUNDED AND SERVED THEM HIMSELF; and the death, which is the one thing no source this folder had gave in full — that Constantius took him for gold received from the emperor and spent on the plague-stricken, tied him to a wild mule and had it driven until he died of his wounds. The Prologue prints no hymn (8 October 2026).

death.note: The folder's first date of any kind: `dates` was null, neither doxologia.ro nor saint.gr giving a year. The Охридски пролог for 31. децембар ст. ст. closes the entry «Пострада у IV веку» — he suffered in the fourth century. The interval is that century and nothing narrower; the entry names Constantine the Great and his son Constantius and gives neither of them a year, and no year was taken from the reigns. Read 8 October 2026.

hymns.text: За любовь Христову, преподобне, нищия возлюбив,/ и сих удоволил еси,/ и Небесное богатство ныне восприял еси, Зотике пребогате./ Сего ради вси тя почитаем,/ совершающе память твою.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 30 декабря ст. ст. — «Кондак священномученика Зотика», глас 2

english.text: For the love of Christ, O venerable one, thou didst love the poor and didst satisfy them, and now thou hast received the wealth of heaven, O most rich Zoticus. Therefore we all honour thee, keeping thy memory.
